content: The Cantonment area was used as a military cantonment during the British Raj in the 19th century. After Indian independence it merged with the rest of Bengaluru while retaining several historic locality and street names and colonial-era architecture.

Domlur was formerly part of the Cantonment area. Public reference material describes it as a location associated with IT outsourcing and military establishments, with Embassy GolfLinks Business Park and HAL Airport located in or near the area.

Indiranagar is described as a residential and commercial neighborhood between the central and eastern parts of Bengaluru. Public reference material notes its cosmopolitan character, nightlife, pubs, retail stores and the commercial importance of 100 Feet Road.
Rajajinagar is a Bengaluru neighborhood established in 1949.
Malleswaram is included as a Central Bengaluru neighborhood in the public Bengaluru neighborhood reference.

The Pete area was established by Kempe Gowda I during the creation of Bangalore and is described as a centre of trade and commercial activity. It contains localities associated with different markets, including Chickpet, Balepet, Cottonpet and Sultanpet.
Sadashivanagar is described as an upscale neighborhood in the heart of Bengaluru.

Seshadripuram was established in 1892 to reduce congestion in the Pete area. Public reference material describes it as primarily residential and notes its educational institutions and Kumara Park extension.
Shivajinagar is one of the older areas of Bengaluru and functions as a major transport junction. Russell Market and Bengaluru Cantonment railway station are noted landmarks.
Ulsoor, also known as Halasuru, is described as one of the older areas of Bengaluru and is known for Ulsoor Lake near MG Road.
Vasanth Nagar is located south of Bengaluru Palace and is described as an upscale neighborhood in the heart of the city. Cunningham Road is a major commercial area associated with the locality.
R. T. Nagar, or Rabindranath Tagore Nagar, is located north of Bengaluru Palace. Public reference material places it within roughly 7 kilometres of Vidhana Soudha.
Bellandur is located along the Outer Ring Road and is described as an IT hub with multiple technology parks and SEZs. Bellandur Lake is also associated with the locality.
C. V. Raman Nagar is described as a neighborhood west of the Outer Ring Road and is associated with Bagmane Tech Park.
Hoodi is described as being close to Whitefield and Outer Ring Road IT hubs. This relationship has contributed to residential and commercial development in the locality.
Krishnarajapuram is located at the northern part of the Outer Ring Road at its junction with Old Madras Road. The locality is also associated with the Krishnarajapuram assembly constituency.
Mahadevapura is described as an IT hub along the Outer Ring Road and was formerly a city municipal council. Phoenix Market City is located in the neighborhood.

Marathahalli is located at the junction of Old Airport Road and the Outer Ring Road. Public reference material notes that it was a village until the 1990s and underwent rapid urbanization during Bengaluru's IT boom.
Varthur is described as a commercial and residential area adjacent to Whitefield.

Whitefield is described as an eastern Bengaluru neighborhood that was formerly a settlement of Anglo-Indians and is now regarded as one of the city's major IT clusters. It houses ITPL and major commercial developments.
Banaswadi is included as a North-Eastern Bengaluru neighborhood in the public neighborhood reference.
HBR Layout is included as a North-Eastern Bengaluru neighborhood in the public neighborhood reference. Official civic material also identifies HBR Layout within Bengaluru's administrative structure.
Horamavu is included as a North-Eastern Bengaluru neighborhood and appears in official Bengaluru civic administrative material.
Kalyan Nagar is included as a North-Eastern Bengaluru neighborhood in the public neighborhood reference.
Kammanahalli is included as a North-Eastern Bengaluru neighborhood. Official civic material also associates the locality with Bengaluru's administrative structure.
Lingarajapuram is included as a North-Eastern Bengaluru neighborhood in the public neighborhood reference.
Ramamurthy Nagar is included as a North-Eastern Bengaluru neighborhood in the public neighborhood reference.
Hebbal is included as a Northern Bengaluru neighborhood and appears in official civic administrative material.
Jalahalli is included as a Northern Bengaluru neighborhood in the public neighborhood reference.
Mathikere is included as a Northern Bengaluru neighborhood in the public neighborhood reference.
Peenya is included as a Northern Bengaluru neighborhood in the public neighborhood reference.
Vidyaranyapura is included as a Northern Bengaluru neighborhood and appears in official civic material.
Yelahanka is included as a Northern Bengaluru neighborhood and is represented in official Bengaluru civic administrative material.
Yeshwanthpur is included as a Northern Bengaluru neighborhood in the public neighborhood reference.
Bommanahalli is described as primarily residential and has undergone commercial growth, with proximity to Electronic City and HSR Layout.
Bommasandra is included in the South-Eastern Bengaluru neighborhood reference.
BTM Layout is described as a commercial and residential neighborhood. It is bounded by or connected with residential areas including Jayanagar, JP Nagar, Madiwala and Bommanahalli.

Electronic City is described as a large industrial area on the outskirts of Bengaluru with offices of major technology companies and other industries. Public reference material also describes the area as being connected to Bengaluru by Hosur Road and notes the Yellow Line metro corridor.
HSR Layout is described as a residential area in Bengaluru located between Hosur Road and Sarjapur Road.
Koramangala is described as a large commercial and residential neighborhood along Hosur Road and as a sought-after real-estate area connecting different parts of Bengaluru.
Madiwala is described as a busy business centre close to Koramangala and is associated with Madiwala Lake.
Banashankari is included as a Southern Bengaluru neighborhood in the public neighborhood reference.
Basavanagudi is included as a Southern Bengaluru neighborhood in the public neighborhood reference.
Girinagar is included as a Southern Bengaluru neighborhood in the public neighborhood reference.
JP Nagar is included as a Southern Bengaluru neighborhood in the public neighborhood reference.
Jayanagar is included as a Southern Bengaluru neighborhood in the public neighborhood reference and is represented in official Bengaluru civic material.
Kumaraswamy Layout is included as a Southern Bengaluru neighborhood in the public neighborhood reference.
Padmanabhanagar is included as a Southern Bengaluru neighborhood in the public neighborhood reference.
Uttarahalli is included as a Southern Bengaluru neighborhood and appears in official civic administrative material.
Anjanapura is included as a Southern Bengaluru suburb in the public neighborhood reference.
Arekere is included as a Southern Bengaluru suburb in the public neighborhood reference.
Begur is included as a Southern Bengaluru suburb and appears in official civic administrative material.
Gottigere is included as a Southern Bengaluru suburb in the public neighborhood reference.
Hulimavu is included as a Southern Bengaluru suburb in the public neighborhood reference.
Kothnur is included as a Southern Bengaluru suburb in the public neighborhood reference.
Basaveshwaranagar is described as a residential locality on the western side of Chord Road and is named after the 12th-century philosopher Basavanna.
Kamakshipalya is described as a neighborhood around the intersection of Magadi Road and the Outer Ring Road.
Kengeri is located along Mysore Road and is described as an important transport hub with a railway station and TTMC. Kengeri Satellite Town was developed by the Bangalore Development Authority.
Mahalakshmi Layout is described as a large western Bengaluru neighborhood near Yeshwantpur and is associated with numerous temples, including ISKCON Temple.

Nagarbhavi is located south of Magadi Road and along the Outer Ring Road. Public reference material notes educational institutions in and around the locality, including Bangalore University and National Law School of India University.
Nandini Layout is included as a Western Bengaluru neighborhood in the public neighborhood reference.

Nayandahalli is described as a transport junction in western Bengaluru. Public reference material associates it with the Mysore Road Satellite Bus Station, Mysore Road metro station and NICE Road junction.

Rajarajeshwari Nagar is located in the south-western part of Bengaluru along Mysore Road. It is described as primarily residential and associated with educational institutions and Global Village Tech Park.
Vijayanagar is a large residential locality bounded by Magadi Road and Mysore Road, with Chord Road running through it. It includes sublocalities such as Chandra Layout and RPC Layout.
Kengeri Satellite Town is described as a township developed by the Bangalore Development Authority and associated with Kengeri in western Bengaluru.
Attibele is listed as a peripheral town associated with the Bengaluru metropolitan area. It lies at the junction of NH44 and SH35 near the Karnataka-Tamil Nadu border.
Anekal is listed as a peripheral town associated with the Bengaluru metropolitan area and lies along SH35.
Chandapura is listed as a peripheral town associated with Bengaluru and lies along NH44.
Thavarekere is listed among peripheral towns associated with the Bengaluru metropolitan area.
Chikkabanavara is listed among peripheral towns associated with Bengaluru and lies along SH39.
Hesaraghatta is listed among peripheral towns associated with Bengaluru and lies along SH39.
Jigani is listed among peripheral towns associated with Bengaluru and lies along SH87.
Nelamangala is listed among peripheral towns associated with Bengaluru and lies along NH48 and NH75.
Sarjapura is listed among peripheral towns associated with Bengaluru and lies along NH648 and SH35 near the Karnataka-Tamil Nadu border.
